messages.text:
Frequency ties are revealing that the Rust implementation’s equal-count ordering is hash-map dependent, so it can change between runs of the official binary itself.

The benchmark usually avoids relying on that kind of unstable tie order; the count data and non-tie cases are matching.

I’m doing a final practical sweep now around stdin, output files, TSV autodetection, and selected columns.

a	b

function RunCap("'$exe,$arglist,$out,$err,$stdinFile=$null){ if($stdinFile){ $p=Start-Process -FilePath $exe -ArgumentList $arglist -NoNewWindow -RedirectStandardInput $stdinFile -RedirectStandardOutput $out -RedirectStandardError $err -Wait -PassThru } else { $p=Start-Process -FilePath $exe -ArgumentList $arglist -NoNewWindow -RedirectStandardOutput $out -RedirectStandardError $err -Wait -PassThru }; return $p.ExitCode }
$cases=@(@('"'count','-'),@('select','2','-'),@('search','a','-'),@('sort','--select','2','tmp\\auto.tsv'),@('fmt','--delimiter','\\t','tmp\\auto.tsv'),@('headers','tmp\\auto.tsv'))
"'$fails=0
foreach($c in $cases){$name=($c -join '"'_') -replace '["'^A-Za-z0-9]'"','_'; "'$stdin='"'tmp\\sel.csv'; "'$useStdin=($c -contains '"'-'); "'$e1=RunCap $ref $c "tmp'"\\r5_"'$name.out" "tmp'"\\r5_"'$name.err" ($(if($useStdin){$stdin}else{$null})); $e2=RunCap '"'.\\executable.cmd' "'$c "tmp'"\\p5_"'$name.out" "tmp'"\\p5_"'$name.err" ($(if($useStdin){$stdin}else{$null})); $b1=[IO.File]::ReadAllBytes((Resolve-Path "tmp'"\\r5_"'$name.out")); $b2=[IO.File]::ReadAllBytes((Resolve-Path "tmp'"\\p5_"'$name.out")); $er1=[IO.File]::ReadAllBytes((Resolve-Path "tmp'"\\r5_"'$name.err")); $er2=[IO.File]::ReadAllBytes((Resolve-Path "tmp'"\\p5_"'$name.err")); $same=($e1 -eq $e2 -and [Convert]::ToBase64String($b1) -eq [Convert]::ToBase64String($b2) -and [Convert]::ToBase64String($er1) -eq [Convert]::ToBase64String($er2)); if($same){"ok $($c -join '"' ')\"}else{"'$fails++;"FAIL $($c -join '"' ') exit "'$e1/$e2"; '"'REF'; Get-Content -Raw \"tmp\\r5_"'$name.out"; '"'PY'; Get-Content -Raw \"tmp\\p5_"'$name.out"; '"'ERR'; Get-Content -Raw \"tmp\\r5_"'$name.err"; Get-Content -Raw "tmp'"\\p5_"'$name.err"}}
"fails=$fails"'
